summary: The code change is correct, minimal, and complete, and I verified every behavioural claim independently rather than from the worker's report. src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs now extracts the final path component as the substring after max(LastIndexOf('/'), LastIndexOf('\\')) with no System.IO reference at all (the 'using System.IO' and the Path.GetFileName call are gone, confirmed by reading the file and by grepping src/ for GetFileName), and the removal predicate IsNonPrintingScalar is an explicit four-category allow-list (Control/Cc, Format/Cf, LineSeparator/Zl, ParagraphSeparator/Zp) evaluated with Rune.GetUnicodeCategory, so it is a strict superset of the pre-fix Rune.IsControl (Cc-only) predicate and cannot remove a legitimate category by side effect. The 128-scalar bound is still applied after removal, the pass is still rune-wise so surrogate pairs are never split, and no collapse or trim was introduced. I reproduced the discriminating pre-fix probe myself in an isolated copy of the tree whose only difference was src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs restored from HEAD (verified still carrying 'Path.GetFileName(primaryPath)' and 'Rune.IsControl(rune)'): Failed 25 / Passed 27 / Total 52, with the exact 18 SEC-21.5-02 and 7 SEC-21.5-03 failures and the right defect in each message (e.g. Actual: "C:\\Users\\admin\\Videos\\secret.mkv" emitted whole, Actual: "C:\\" instead of the item id, 'mo<U+202E>vie.mkv'); the working tree was never mutated and still carries the fix. I re-ran the focused LogSubjectTests (52/52), LogRedactionTests (167/167), ./build.sh build (0 warnings, 0 errors), the default suite (0 / 1966 / 66 / 2032) and the host-guarded suite against the pinned host at /tmp/arrtags-14.3/jellyfin, whose Jellyfin.Api.dll product version I verified as 12+6c073e19ddf604b2369c638716164fdab4c952dc (0 / 1986 / 46 / 2032). I also drove the shipped LogSubject directly from a scratch console program against the built ArrTags.dll to probe the category set and the extraction in both directions: Co, Mc, Mn, Zs (U+0020, U+00A0, U+3000, U+2000), Cn, regional indicators, letters and a lone surrogate are all preserved; Cc, Cf (U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF, U+FFF9), Zl and Zp are all removed; a backslash inside the final component truncates ('ac\\dc.mkv' -> 'dc.mkv'), a trailing separator and a UNC host-only value behave as documented, and 300 plain scalars truncate to exactly 128 while 200 astral scalars after a removed Cf yield 128 scalars / 256 UTF-16 units. No new secret, directory, drive, share, parent chain, or unbounded value can reach the log through the change: LogSubject is the single chooser of the subject for all eight call sites (verified by grepping src/), the emitted value is either a separator-free bounded component or the D-format item id, and the widened predicate can only shrink a subject or trigger the already-allowed item-id fallback. Scope and documentation are also clean where the task required them: 9 modified files, no golden/RenderVersion/renderer-schema/dependency/configuration change, ADR-026's Decision section byte-identical (diff of the '### Decision' block against HEAD is empty, the whole diff is 40 insertions / 0 deletions, and lines 1-140 including the 15.1-15.4 note are byte-identical), architecture 06 and 12 no longer say host-platform-scoped or Cc-only, architecture 07 and 11 contain no equivalent statement, README and the changelog are accurate, and PLANS.md/state.json are consistent (render-docs-state --check: 'PLANS.md and state.json agree'). All nine acceptance criteria are met. The one required change is a documentation accuracy defect, not a behaviour defect: docs/decisions/ADR-020.md's 'Amendment note (v1.2, ADR-026; task 15.4)' still asserts, as a current statement of the shipped redaction contract, that the subject is 'the file-name component only (`Path.GetFileName`)' and that 'The path exclusion is a host-native-path statement: the subject uses the host-platform `Path.GetFileName` semantics, so on the pinned Linux host ... a Windows-style backslash string is a single file name rather than a path'. Both statements are now false about the shipped code, ADR-020 owns the clause 4 redaction contract that ADR-026 amends, and nothing anywhere in ADR-020 points forward to the change (grep for '21.11' in ADR-020.md returns nothing), so the supersession the new ADR-026 note performs is incomplete. This is the same wording class the task required to be corrected in architecture 06/12 and the README, on the same decision surface, and the project's own precedent (SR-15.4-02, SR2-15.4-05) treats exactly this as a defect. The fix is one appended, purely additive note; no clause text needs to be edited and no user decision is required. A second, contract-level item is informational only: check-docs.sh currently fails on the two contract-mandated agent-report pairing lines for 21.11, which clears when the orchestrator lists this reviewer report and the test-quality review in the task's state.json reports array (the pattern task 21.7 used). An earlier review pass over this task produced no persisted report, so this file is the first persisted implementation-reviewer report for 21.11.

findings.area: documentation / current-state accuracy on a canonical decision surface
findings.summary: docs/decisions/ADR-020.md's v1.2 amendment note still states the pre-fix host-platform `Path.GetFileName` semantics and the 'a Windows-style backslash string is a single file name rather than a path' scope as the shipped redaction contract, which this change makes false, and nothing in ADR-020 points forward to the new ADR-026 note.
findings.detail: The task's required work includes 'Update the documentation wording that the fix makes stale, without rewriting ADR decision text', and the worker executed that for ADR-026 (an appended task 21.11 implementation note that explicitly supersedes the task 15.1-15.4 note's 'Cc-only' and 'host-native-path' readings) and for architecture sections 06 and 12 and the README. The same sweep was not carried across to ADR-020, which carries the identical pre-fix wording in its own '### Amendment note (v1.2, ADR-026; task 15.4)' section: line 100-102 'when a primary media path is available, the file-name component only (`Path.GetFileName`), bounded to at most 128 Unicode scalar values and with control scalars removed', and lines 121-124 'The path exclusion is a host-native-path statement: the subject uses the host-platform `Path.GetFileName` semantics, so on the pinned Linux host a POSIX media path yields the file-name component, while a Windows-style backslash string is a single file name rather than a path.' After this change both statements are false about the code: LogSubject contains no System.IO reference and ExtractFinalComponent splits on '/' and '\\' on every host, so a Windows-style or UNC path no longer yields one file name, and the predicate is Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp rather than 'control scalars'. ADR-020 is the ADR that owns the clause 4 redaction contract ADR-026 amends, and the project's 15.4 work deliberately recorded the host-native scope 'consistently across the ADRs' (ADR-020, ADR-026, architecture 06/12, README, PLANS risk row), so the correction was expected to be consistent there too; the supersession note added to ADR-026 claims to supersede 'two reading-level statements in the task 15.1-15.4 implementation note above' and so does not reach the copies in ADR-020. Consequence for the release chain: a reader of ADR-020 alone (or a security reviewer tracing the clause 4 exclusion in 21.14) gets a wrong picture of the shipped exclusion, and two decision records describe the same contract differently. This is a documentation-accuracy defect, not a behavioural one: nothing in the plugin depends on it, and no user decision is needed. The project's precedent treats this class as a real defect (the 15.4 security review raised the identical README/architecture-06 over-claim as SR-15.4-02 and it was corrected; SR2-15.4-05 closed the same way by amending docs/limitations/accepted.md SEC-5).

findings.area: correctness / documented consequence of the mandated category set
findings.summary: Widening the predicate to Cf removes U+200D/U+200C, so an emoji ZWJ sequence in a legitimate file name is emitted with the joiner gone; this is a correlation-key fidelity consequence, bounded and secret-free, mandated by the task's category floor and owned by the 21.14 review's over-removal adjudication.
findings.detail: Direct probe of the shipped LogSubject: '/media/Movies/Movie <U+1F468><U+200D><U+1F469><U+200D><U+1F467>.mkv' is emitted as 'Movie <U+1F468><U+1F469><U+1F467>.mkv' (13 scalars), so the rendered glyphs differ from the on-disk name. U+200C ZWNJ, U+FEFF and U+FFF9 are removed the same way. This is a real instance of the over-removal risk the corrective record names ('a category added to the predicate that a legitimate media file name uses ... silently corrupts the operator's correlation key'), but Cf was the task's explicit floor ('at minimum Cc, Cf, Zl, Zp'), the worker documented the preserved categories explicitly rather than leaving the set implicit as the task required, and the corrective record assigns the two-direction over/under-removal probe to task 21.14. The subject is still bounded to 128 scalars, still contains no separator and no directory component, and the alternative (keeping the joiner) would leave the reproduced log-integrity defect open, so no change is required here.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 1. A Cf/Zl/Zp scalar in a file-name component does not survive into the emitted subject, and an ordinary Cc control is still stripped (superset).
acceptance_criteria.evidence: IsNonPrintingScalar (LogSubject.cs:139-146) matches exactly Control, Format, LineSeparator and ParagraphSeparator via Rune.GetUnicodeCategory, so it is a strict superset of Rune.IsControl (Cc). UnicodeNonPrintingScalarsAreRemoved covers U+202E/U+200B/U+200D/U+00AD/U+202A/U+202C/U+2066/U+2069/U+2028/U+2029 and NonPrintingRemovalStillRemovesOrdinaryControlScalars mixes U+202E with U+0001/U+0000; the first ten fail on the pre-fix source in my own probe. My independent probe additionally confirms U+200C, U+FEFF and U+FFF9 are removed while Co, Mc, Mn, Zs (U+0020/U+00A0/U+3000/U+2000), Cn, letters and regional indicators are preserved, so no legitimate category is stripped.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 2. 'C:\\Users\\admin\\Videos\\secret.mkv' -> 'secret.mkv' with no backslash/account/directory; same for UNC and mixed-separator paths on any host.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: ExtractFinalComponent (LogSubject.cs:83-87) is the only component chooser and uses Math.Max(LastIndexOf('/'), LastIndexOf('\\')) with no System.IO reference (the 'using System.IO' and the Path.GetFileName call are removed). FinalComponentIsTakenOnBothSeparators covers the drive, UNC, mixed, relative-backslash and '/media\\Movies/mixed.mkv' rows, and WindowsStylePathEmitsNoAccountOrDirectoryComponent additionally asserts no '\\', 'admin', 'Users', 'Videos' or 'C:'. My pre-fix probe shows the drive, UNC and relative rows failing with the whole path emitted, and my post-fix probe reproduces 'C:/Users\\admin/Videos/secret.mkv' -> 'secret.mkv' and '\\\\server' -> 'server'. Host-independence is structural (no platform API), and grep over src/ shows no other GetFileName use in the logging path.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 3. The 128-scalar bound still holds after removal (300-scalar name -> exactly 128), surrogate pairs never split, whitespace never collapsed/trimmed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The single pass is unchanged except for the predicate: it enumerates runes, skips removed scalars, and only then applies the appended == MaximumScalarValues break, so removal precedes the bound. BoundIsAppliedAfterNonPrintingRemoval asserts exactly 128 'a' scalars after 300 removed scalars; WidenedRemovalStillNeverSplitsASurrogatePair asserts 128 astral scalars / 256 UTF-16 units. My own probe against the built assembly: 300 plain scalars -> 128 scalars/128 UTF-16; 200 astral scalars after a leading U+202E -> 128 scalars/256 UTF-16 with the trailing 'b' run cut by the bound. Whitespace is neither collapsed nor trimmed: '/media/Movies/my <U+202E> movie .mkv' -> 'my  movie .mkv' and my probe shows '  a.mkv  ' keeps its surrounding spaces. (The test-quality review's TQ-21.11-02 notes no committed case observes the no-trim half; the behaviour itself is verified here by direct probe.)

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 4. Empty/whitespace/separator-only/reduces-to-nothing paths still fall back to the item id in D format.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Create keeps both guards: the pre-normalization IsNullOrWhiteSpace check is now re-run on the extracted component (LogSubject.cs:59-62) and the post-normalization check remains at line 69. WindowsStyleSeparatorOnlyPathsFallBackToTheItemIdentifier covers 'C:\\', '\\\\fileserver\\share\\', '\\' and '\\/', NamesThatReduceToNothingAfterNonPrintingRemovalFallBackToTheItemIdentifier covers the Cf-only and space-plus-Cf names, and FallbackIsTheItemIdentifierInDFormat pins length 36 + TryParseExact + value equality. My probe confirms 'C:' + backslash, '\\server\\name\\' (trailing separator) and the Cf-only name all take the D-format fallback.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: 5. The removal category set is stated in code docs and in the ADR-026 note.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: The NormalizeFileName XML doc (LogSubject.cs:89-102) and the IsNonPrintingScalar XML doc (lines 131-137) both name exactly Cc, Cf, Zl, Zp and name the preserved categories (Mn, Zs, Co, Cn, letters, emoji). The ADR-026 'Implementation note (v1.2, task 21.11: SEC-21.5-02 and SEC-21.5-03)' states the same four categories with the reproduced scalar list, the dual-separator extraction, and the preserved bounds and fallback. The class summary and the primaryPath param doc state the platform-independent extraction.
